subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as a public per-agent config contract, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 remain the landing path?
rationale: The source-reproduced gap is real, but adding these per-agent blocks changes strict config validation, context/session behavior, and provider/auth routing, so automation should not create a competing fix without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor additive per-agent overrides
options.body: Approve the config direction, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR as the repair or replacement path.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model first
options.body: Accept only `agents.list[].compaction.model` initially and defer broader compaction and context-pruning knobs to a later design issue.

options.title: Keep defaults-only behavior
options.body: Decline the config expansion and close or redirect implementation PRs, leaving users to use global defaults or separate deployments.

recommendation.title: Sponsor additive per-agent overrides
recommendation.body: Approve the config direction, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR as the repair or replacement path.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned on the open implementation PR that currently owns the decision path.
